sources.facts: Lists us-261025.osm.pbf at 12229320016 bytes; declares latest publisher state 2026-10-25T21:21:21Z. That state is a proposed header requirement, not yet observed in the dated PBF.
Daily extracts use publisher clipping polygons; public data omits user/uid/changeset. No new global completeness or exact historical reconstruction claim follows.
Streaming object views expire when processing advances; retained native fields must be copied. Repeated reading/caching resolves references.
FileProcessor supports streaming; location caching defaults to flex_mem if enabled. Proposed reader deliberately avoids that national in-memory cache.
Headers expose options and readers expose EOF/header access. Exact available source fields must be checked, not inferred.
Captured metadata identifies the CPython3.13 Linux aarch64 wheel, size and SHA256; requests is the runtime dependency. Other listed extras are not requested. No wheel was fetched.

max_page_count bounds a database file; cache_size is a suggested cache limit, not a process-memory guarantee. mmap_size=0 disables mapped IO. temp_store may be affected by build options. OFF journals can leave corrupt derived indexes after errors/crashes; no recovery/resume may rely on them. PRAGMAs must be read back because unknown statements can be ignored.

Requires BlobHeader under64KiB and uncompressed Blob under32MiB; raw/zlib are required encodings. Replication timestamp identifies database replication state, not a guarantee every object with an earlier timestamp is included. Proposed v2 uses publisher replication-state identity, not the old global time-query identity.
